questions.question: Calculate the number of moles present in 12.0 g of carbon (C). [A_r: C = 12]
questions.explanation: Moles = frac{mass}{M_r} = frac{12.0}{12.0} = 1.0 mol.

questions.question: Calculate the mass, in grams, of 0.50 moles of water (H_2O). [A_r: H = 1, O = 16]
A student weighs out 11.1 g of anhydrous calcium chloride (CaCl_2). Calculate the number of moles used. [A_r: Ca = 40, Cl = 35.5]
What is the mass of 2.50 moles of sulfuric acid (H_2SO_4)? [A_r: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
Calculate the number of moles of oxygen atoms present in 4.6 g of nitrogen dioxide (NO_2). [A_r: N = 14, O = 16]
questions.explanation: M_r of NO_2 = 14 + 2(16) = 46. Moles of NO_2 = frac{4.6}{46} = 0.10 mol. Each NO_2 has 2 O atoms, so moles of O = 0.10 × 2 = 0.20 mol.

questions.question: Which sample contains a greater number of moles: 10.0 g of NaOH or 10.0 g of KOH? [A_r: Na = 23, K = 39, O = 16, H = 1]
options: NaOH, because it has a lower M_r
KOH, because it has a higher M_r
Both contain the same number of moles
questions.explanation: Moles = frac{mass}{M_r}. For the same mass, the compound with the lower M_r (NaOH, M_r = 40) will have more moles than the one with the higher M_r (KOH, M_r = 56).

questions.question: A sample of an unknown gas has a mass of 8.8 g and contains exactly 0.20 moles. Calculate its M_r and suggest its identity.
questions.explanation: M_r = frac{mass}{moles} = frac{8.8}{0.20} = 44. The common carbon oxide with M_r = 44 is CO_2 (12 + 2(16) = 44).

questions.question: Calculate the exact mass of 0.100 moles of hydrated copper(II) sulfate (CuSO_4·5H_2O). [A_r: Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
1.00 g of a Group 2 metal carbonate (XCO_3) contains 0.010 moles. Calculate the A_r of metal X and identify it. [A_r: C = 12, O = 16]
Calculate the volume, in dm^3, occupied by 0.50 moles of oxygen gas (O_2) at r.t.p.
questions.explanation: Volume = moles × 24 dm^3 = 0.50 × 24 = 12.0 dm^3.

questions.question: A gas syringe collects 4.80 dm^3 of hydrogen gas (H_2) at r.t.p. Calculate the number of moles collected.
questions.explanation: Moles = frac{volume}{24} = frac{4.80}{24} = 0.20 mol.

questions.question: What is the volume, in cm^3, of 0.020 moles of carbon dioxide (CO_2) at r.t.p.?
Calculate the mass of 1.20 dm^3 of sulfur dioxide (SO_2) gas at r.t.p. [A_r: S = 32, O = 16]
Flask A contains 4.0 g of helium (He) and Flask B contains 4.0 g of methane (CH_4). Both are at r.t.p. Which flask contains the larger volume of gas?
options: Flask A, because He has fewer moles
Flask A, because He has more moles
Flask B, because CH_4 has a higher M_r
questions.explanation: Moles of He = frac{4.0}{4} = 1.0 mol. Moles of CH_4 = frac{4.0}{16} = 0.25 mol. Flask A has more moles, hence a larger volume.

questions.question: 0.10 mol of solid calcium carbonate (CaCO_3) is heated strongly until it completely decomposes. Calculate the maximum volume of CO_2 produced at r.t.p.
questions.explanation: CaCO_3 → CaO + CO_2. Molar ratio is 1:1. Moles of CO_2 = 0.10 mol. Volume = 0.10 × 24 = 2.4 dm^3.

questions.question: A student vaporizes a liquid and collects 240 cm^3 of its gas at r.t.p. If the mass is 0.60 g, calculate the M_r of the liquid.
questions.explanation: Volume = 240 cm^3 = 0.24 dm^3. Moles = frac{0.24}{24} = 0.010 mol. M_r = frac{mass}{moles} = frac{0.60}{0.010} = 60.

questions.question: A gas mixture contains 0.10 mol of O_2 and 0.20 mol of N_2. Calculate the total volume of this mixture at r.t.p.
questions.explanation: Total moles = 0.10 + 0.20 = 0.30 mol. Total volume = 0.30 × 24 = 7.2 dm^3.

questions.question: A student wishes to collect exactly 0.0050 moles of hydrogen gas at r.t.p. What volume, in cm^3, should they aim to collect?
Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm^3, of a solution containing 0.20 moles of NaCl dissolved in 0.50 dm^3 of water.
questions.explanation: Concentration = frac{moles}{volume} = frac{0.20}{0.50} = 0.40 mol/dm^3.

questions.question: A solution of HCl has a concentration of 2.0 mol/dm^3. Calculate the number of moles of HCl present in 250 cm^3 of this solution.
questions.explanation: Volume = 250 cm^3 = 0.25 dm^3. Moles = concentration × volume = 2.0 × 0.25 = 0.50 mol.

questions.question: 4.0 g of solid NaOH is dissolved in water to make exactly 200 cm^3 of solution. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm^3. [A_r: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: M_r of NaOH = 40. Moles = frac{4.0}{40} = 0.10 mol. Volume = 200 cm^3 = 0.20 dm^3. Concentration = frac{0.10}{0.20} = 0.50 mol/dm^3.

questions.question: Convert a concentration of 0.50 mol/dm^3 of H_2SO_4 into g/dm^3. [A_r: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: M_r of H_2SO_4 = 98. Concentration in g/dm^3 = mol/dm^3 × M_r = 0.50 × 98 = 49.0 g/dm^3.

questions.question: A commercial bottle of aqueous ammonia (NH_3) has a concentration of 34.0 g/dm^3. Calculate its concentration in mol/dm^3. [A_r: N = 14, H = 1]
questions.explanation: M_r of NH_3 = 14 + 3(1) = 17. Concentration in mol/dm^3 = frac{34.0}{17} = 2.0 mol/dm^3.

questions.question: 50.0 cm^3 of a 2.0 mol/dm^3 CuSO_4 solution is diluted with water to a total volume of 500 cm^3. Calculate the new concentration.
questions.explanation: Moles of CuSO_4 = 2.0 × (frac{50}{1000}) = 0.10 mol. New volume = 500 cm^3 = 0.50 dm^3. New concentration = frac{0.10}{0.50} = 0.20 mol/dm^3.
